images.author: Nyttend
images.caption: Front and northern side of the Bates-Cockrem House, located at 325 Lawrence Street in Sandusky, Ohio, United States.  Built in 1840, it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

brief: A resort-town cottage lot: Bates-Cockrem House, a 19th-century lake-town house. One photo; year estimated. Older than 1970: northern Michigan resort cottages of this kind are 1880-1950 buildings; Commons has almost no newer ones. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the Bates-Cockrem House (Sandusky OH, 1840s-80s): a two-storey side-gabled house of coursed grey limestone with dressed lintels, 6/6 sash, a columned entry portico; clipped shrubs

why.note: Sandusky's own limestone: the 'Stone City' of Lake Erie, quarried under the town
